deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematical derivations. It is the title page and opening of Riemann's natural-philosophy fragment. A closely related, fuller text appears among the philosophical fragments ('Naturphilosophie') in Weber/Dedekind's edition of the Gesammelte Werke.

Title: 'Versuch einer Lehre von den Grundbegriffen der Mathematik und Physik als Grundlage für die Naturerklärung' (Attempt at a theory of the fundamental concepts of mathematics and physics as a foundation for the explanation of nature).

The page makes three programmatic theses.
(1) Natural science is the attempt to grasp nature through precise concepts.
(2) The concepts through which we grasp nature do two things. At every moment they supplement our perceptions. They also determine future perceptions 'as necessary'. On this sheet the sentence breaks off here. In the fuller published version, Riemann goes on to say that where the conceptual system is insufficient, future perceptions are determined as probable.
(3) It is therefore important to search out the origin of these concepts in our apprehension of nature. Only in this way can their meaning be fixed adequately for the explanation of nature. The first question to investigate is how new concepts are formed, where this is open to observation. Equivalently: what is the path by which natural science advances?

Context from the previous sheet (the same complex of drafts): Riemann goes on to discuss the following.
- The formation of the concept of things existing for themselves.
- The conflict between that concept and change.
- The resulting twin concepts of continuous change and of causality.
- The question whether a change happens through very many imperceptible jumps or through all intermediate stages. Riemann prefers continuity, in order to preserve the concept of persisting things as far as possible.

This is the epistemological programme behind Riemann's view that concepts are corrected by expectations being disappointed. It connects to his Habilitation lecture's remarks on the empirical status of geometric hypotheses.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible; the page is purely philosophical prose. The second sentence is left incomplete on this sheet. It ends with 'als nothwendig' and lacks the verb ('vorausbestimmt') and the continuation found in the published version.

results.what: Programmatic definition of natural science as grasping nature through precise concepts, which both supplement present perceptions and predetermine future ones.
results.modern_name: Riemann's epistemology of natural science (conceptual systems as predictive, corrected by experience)
results.usually_credited_to: Bernhard Riemann, 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts', Gesammelte Werke (1876)

results.what: Methodological demand to study the origin of concepts, i.e. how new concepts are formed and how science advances, as the way to fix their meaning.
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (influenced by J. F. Herbart); published in Werke
